title: Why Pakistan's fuel prices now change every few days
credits: Photos: Shujaat Muzaffar, Chris LeBoutillier / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Pakistan has changed the way it sets fuel prices, and diesel has just gone up again.
The price of high-speed diesel has risen by one rupee ninety-one paisa, to three hundred and ninety-three rupees sixty-six paisa a litre.
Petrol stays at three hundred and seventy-seven rupees seventy-one paisa a litre.
Diesel matters most to the wider economy, because it powers trucks, buses, tractors and generators.
The government has now moved to daily price reviews, because of volatility in world oil markets.
Prices will follow a rolling seven-day average of international prices.
Pakistan used to change fuel prices every two weeks, and then every week.
The government says any change in the petroleum levy must stay within the limit approved by the cabinet.
World oil prices have swung sharply this month, as attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz hit a record.
Brent crude climbed above one hundred and seventeen dollars a barrel last week.
For Pakistani families, that means fuel bills could change more often than ever.
